final.executive_summary: Hold AAPL at ~3% of total account equity — retain the existing 9.6227 shares (~$2,940 of the $99,846 account) with no transaction at the 2026-08-17 signal close. The three risk seats independently converged on the same 3% total target and the same reasoning structure (own both tails, size for the binary FQ4 gross-margin guide), so the decision is not a compromise: it is the only size that survives the evidence. The higher alternative of 6-8% is rejected because adding into the 313.33-333.43 VWMA/gap supply shelf at ~34x peak margins ahead of a binary October guide with no 50M+ accumulation bar is paying up for confirmation already available at 313.33; the lower alternative of 0% is rejected because the filed FQ3 FY26 evidence (revenue +16.5%, gross margin 50.05% +356bps, EPS +28.7%) shows no margin deterioration, price is +8.88% above a rising 200 SMA at 280.67, and cash in this account earns zero. Treat 298 as an end-of-day decision level (not an intraday stop, ~1.0 ATR), not an order; add only on a >50M-share close above 313.33 (raise total target to ~6%) or a defended 300.00-302.56 retest that closes back above 305 on expanding volume (~5%); cut to 0 on a close below 298.
final.investment_thesis:
What decided the call. The margin question is won by the bulls on filed evidence, not inference: FQ3 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-06-27) shows revenue +16.5% against cost of revenue +8.6%, gross margin 50.05% (+356bps), operating margin +263bps and diluted EPS +28.7% to $2.02 (9M EPS $6.88, +22.4%). The bear's margin-reversion case — a +260% raw-materials build to $7,645M against finished goods −4%, with inventory days roughly doubling from ~9.5 to ~18.5 — is a smart inference about a forward cost environment (and the Jefferies note and WSJ supply-chain report are journalistic, with no volumes, suppliers, timelines or cost figures), but inference cannot outrank an observed 50.05% print where COGS grew at half the rate of revenue. The valuation question is won by the bears: ~34x a realistic FY26 EPS near $8.90 (≈38x the FQ3 run-rate) for a hardware-led business at an all-time-high gross margin that ran 38-47% for a decade, after a ~4-turn de-rating from the 07-28 peak, is not a discount, and $62.2bn of net cash is only ~1.4% of a ~$4.46tn market cap — this is an earnings-multiple debate, not a balance-sheet debate. The tape question is won narrowly by the bears over a two-week horizon: 305.59 sits below the 50 SMA (309.08, six consecutive declines), below the 10 EMA (308.76) and below VWMA (311.96), with a 314-333 supply shelf left by the 07-31 gap on 132.5M shares; the bull's MACD-histogram contraction (−3.634 to −2.290) and the lightest volume in 40 sessions (28.23M on 08-14) are real, but 'volume dries up at lows' and 'demand vacuum' are observationally identical until a 50M+ up-day prints, and there is 8.88% of air to the 200 SMA at 280.67. The franchise question is conceded by both sides: $110.2bn of 9M FCF (honestly normalized to ~20% OCF growth after the cash-tax benefit), buyback re-accelerated to ~$25.1bn at only 67% of FCF, zero new long-term debt, deferred revenue +8.8%, R&D +32.5% funded out of gross-margin expansion. Because the strongest arguments cancel on the only question that matters today — whether to commit more capital at 305.59 — a Hold is the committed conclusion, not a refuge from disagreement. Both analysts' own cited research lands on 'neutral / no new exposure at 305.59', and the decision levels (a high-volume reclaim of 313.33 or a close below 300, with the FQ4 gross-margin guide in late October as the arbiter) are shared.

Sizing judged independently of the existing 9.62 shares. The chosen total target is ~3% of total equity (retaining the current 2.945%, ~$2,940), and both the higher and lower bounds are concrete. The higher alternative is 6-8%: it captures the fundamental case and reduces the zero-yield cash drag, but it means adding into a VWMA supply shelf at peak-margin multiples ahead of a binary guide with no accumulation footprint — rejected. The lower alternative is 0%: liquidate and wait for 300 or 313.33 — rejected because the primary trend is intact (price +8.88% above a rising 200 SMA), earnings are compounding in the high-20s, buyback capacity is large and unused, and full liquidation would be a bet that the filed margin evidence reverses, which no supplied evidence supports. The trade-offs are nameable in dollar terms. Cash opportunity cost: with ~97% of the account in zero-yield cash, if AAPL reclaims 313.33 and runs to 333.43 (+9.1%), a 3% position returns ~0.27% of the account versus ~0.7% at 8% — an explicit ~0.4% forgone, which is the price of refusing to underwrite peak margins at 34x before October. Downside: if the FQ4 guide lands in the high 48s on memory costs and 300 breaks toward 280.67 (−8.2%), the same 3% position costs ~0.24-0.27% of the account. The retained position is not an observation token — observing evidence does not require holding stock — it is a genuine two-way exposure of roughly ±0.27% of total equity per ±9% move in AAPL, with round-trip friction of roughly $3 (10bps), which is immaterial in both directions and is not used as an argument either way. No further proportional trim will be applied to a position already at 3%; any size change must come from a fresh total-target judgment tied to a named trigger.

Prior lessons applied. The record here is unambiguous that trimming a structurally rising AAPL on momentum decay alone is expensive: the 2026-06-30, 07-01, 07-13, 07-20, 07-21 and 07-22 Underweights each gave up +3.2% to +6.2% of five-day alpha, and the 2026-08-10 Underweight (−0.9% raw, −0.8% alpha over five days) was inside a single day's ATR of ~2.9% and therefore never evidence of anything. The binding lessons are: (a) a five-day alpha smaller than one ATR is not a verdict, so judge this call at the 300 floor test with volume or the late-October FQ4 print, not on a noise window; and (b) do not leave de-risking or adds to limits that may never fill when price sits just below a defined event. Both point to keeping the shares and pre-committing the levels rather than trading the middle of a 300-313 box.

What would change it. Upgrades: a daily close above 313.33 on volume >50M with the MACD histogram turning positive reclaims the 314-333 shelf and neutralizes the distribution read — raise the total target to ~6% (~$6,000); a defended 300.00-302.56 retest that closes back above 305 on expanding volume supports ~5% (a mere touch of 300 without recovery does not qualify — do not add into a falling tape). Downgrades: a daily close below 298 (beneath the triple-tested 300.00/302.56/300.57 base, beneath the 61.8% retracement at 299.95) cuts the total target to 0 and exits; a close below the rising 200 SMA at 280.67 is full thesis invalidation and confirms the bear's normalization scenario. The single most important scheduled event is the late-October FQ4 gross-margin guide: at or above the 50.05% FQ3 print and framed as structural (Services mix, component pre-buy), the multiple is defensible; a guide in the high 48s confirms reversion and argues for exiting even without a technical break. Stated gaps, not papered over: no quantified cost impact from the WSJ component report; no disclosed methodology, rating basis or multiple behind the Jefferies $263.66 target; no terms or regulatory status for the China/Alibaba AI arrangement; no composition detail for the $13.3bn intangible addition; no actual FQ4 company guidance; and no valuation-multiple series supplied. Until those exist, ~3% is the largest AAPL exposure I can justify against total account equity — not because the evidence is balanced in a way that forbids a call, but because the one question that would move size decisively (margin durability) is answerable only by a print that has not yet occurred.
final.time_horizon: 1-3 months, tactical; re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 gross-margin guide and the 300/313.33 decision levels
